evals.name: draft-and-surface-not-interview
evals.prompt: You are the CPO. Author the PRD for the mailmate project. Its binding is at skills/cpo/.claude/skills/product-prd/evals/inputs/mailmate/project.md — read it, resolve its Product path, and read the product request under it. Draft what you can and surface whatever you can't settle.

assertions.name: three-bucket-companion
assertions.description: A companion file PRD_open_issues.md is produced (separate from PRD.md) and contains all three bucket labels: 'Open issues', 'Choices to confirm', and 'Directives'. All three must be present. A baseline agent typically writes a single PRD and does not split out a three-bucket companion file.

assertions.name: status-draft
assertions.description: The produced PRD.md has a 'Status:' line reading 'Draft' (unresolved items remain) — not 'Settled' or 'Locked'.

assertions.name: confirm-or-override-slot
assertions.description: Each 'Choices to confirm' item in the produced PRD_open_issues.md carries the skill's named per-choice slot label 'Confirm or override:' — the literal phrase 'Confirm or override' appears at least once as an item slot. This is the skill's companion contract; a baseline agent improvises ad-hoc confirmation phrasings (e.g. 'Confirm?', 'Your call:') and does not emit this named slot.

evals.name: reentry-trails-answered-cycle
evals.prompt: You are the CPO. Continue the PRD for the mailmate project. Its binding is at skills/cpo/.claude/skills/product-prd/evals/inputs/mailmate-reentry/project.md; under its Product path the owner has answered the open issues inline in PRD_open_issues.md. Fold their answers in and keep going.

assertions.name: trails-cycle-1
assertions.description: A file trail/prd/cycle-1.md is produced, holding the owner's answered companion copied whole (the first trail cycle is cycle-1). A baseline agent folding answers would not preserve the answered file to a numbered trail cycle.

assertions.name: answers-folded
assertions.description: The produced PRD.md folds in the owner's answers from the answered companion: it states the target segment as SMB support teams (2-10 seats) and a data-retention story of purging thread content roughly 90 days after a thread closes. A baseline agent, which never saw the answered companion, would not carry these specific resolved values.

evals.name: directive-gate-confirm-not-perform
evals.prompt: You are the CPO. Author the PRD for the mailmate project (binding at skills/cpo/.claude/skills/product-prd/evals/inputs/mailmate/project.md). The product request flags an enterprise SLA whose numbers only the infra vendor's account rep can provide — handle that the way the process dictates.

assertions.name: surfaced-as-gate
assertions.description: The enterprise-SLA item is surfaced as a directive / gate — the produced companion (Directives bucket) or the PRD's Gates section names the action, who performs it (the infra vendor's account rep / owner), and what it gates. A baseline agent would either invent SLA numbers or omit the gap.

assertions.name: no-fabricated-numbers
assertions.description: The produced PRD.md does not state specific SLA figures (e.g. '99.9% uptime' or a numeric response-time) as settled fact for the unpublished values — the unknown external number is surfaced, not fabricated.

assertions.name: gate-lifecycle-performed-field
assertions.description: The surfaced enterprise-SLA directive in the produced PRD_open_issues.md carries the skill's gate-lifecycle marker — a 'Performed?' field recording the action as not-yet-done (the confirm-not-perform behavior). The literal 'Performed?' slot is present on the directive. A baseline agent names the directive and who actions it but omits this lifecycle field; it does not track performed-status.

evals.name: tag-external-source-with-locator
evals.prompt: You are the CPO. Author the PRD for the mailmate project (binding at skills/cpo/.claude/skills/product-prd/evals/inputs/mailmate/project.md). It relies on Stripe for billing — reflect what Stripe actually supports.

assertions.name: external-tag-format
assertions.description: A claim in the produced PRD.md that rests on the external Stripe source carries the tag form 'verified (external):' followed by a locator (a URL or a named source), not a bare 'verified'. This 'verified (external)' convention is the skill's tag contract; a baseline agent does not use it.

assertions.name: product-fact-in-body-not-working
assertions.description: The produced PRD.md states the Stripe billing capability as a product fact in the body (what the product requires of billing), while the source locator rides on the tag — the body does not recite the check's working (read-date, sample counts, API-mechanism detail).

evals.name: posture-halt-outside-cpo
evals.prompt: Can you write me a PRD for an email-triage app I'm thinking about?

assertions.name: no-prd-file
assertions.description: No PRD.md file is produced anywhere in the run's outputs — neither in the product root nor beside it. An agent given this prompt has no resolved Product path and may write PRD.md at the outputs root; a PRD written anywhere in the outputs tree counts as produced, so check the tree itself, not only run_delta.json (which watches the product root alone). The skill halts on the CPO-posture check and writes no PRD. A capable baseline agent given this prompt would write a PRD.md file somewhere — so the absence of one anywhere in the outputs tree is the halt signal.

assertions.name: no-companion-file
assertions.description: No PRD_open_issues.md companion file is produced anywhere in the run's outputs either — the skill stops at the posture check before authoring anything. For a posture-halt case, the absence of any authored artifact anywhere in the outputs tree is the correct, expected signal; a file written outside the product root still counts as authored.
